Description: Compact high-field tokamak using HTS REBCO magnets (12+ T). Improved confinement scaling in smaller device footprint. Quasi-steady-state via bootstrap current and external drive.
University / Lab Experiments: ITER, JET (Culham), EAST (ASIPP), JT-60SA (QST/F4E), KSTAR (KFE), DIII-D (GA), Alcator C-Mod (MIT)

Description: Sound-driven implosion of gas bubbles in liquid to extreme temperatures. Single-bubble sonoluminescence creates picosecond UV flashes and dense plasma. Bridge from demonstrated sonoluminescence to thermonuclear conditions is undemonstrated.

Ultrafast Yb:YAG thin-disk laser at kHz rep rate driving structured Laguerre-Gaussian beams into continuous liquid D2O jet. Claims D-D primary with D-T bootstrap burn. Eliminates discrete target fabrication.
University / Lab Experiments: None directly analogous. LG beam physics: Wang et al. 2015 (PIC simulation). Sonoluminescence jet compression has some overlap.

Description: Stellarator using arrays of simple planar HTS coils instead of complex 3D-shaped windings. Simplifies manufacturing at the cost of requiring many more coils. Steady-state.

Z-machine class pulsed power compresses pre-magnetized fuel. Pacific Fusion uses self-magnetizing targets — axial seed field generated by the drive current itself, eliminating external premagnetization coils. Impedance-matched Marx generator arrays drive the high-current pulses.
University / Lab Experiments: Sandia Z Machine (MagLIF experiments), NRL (magnetized ICF)

Description: Two FRC plasmoids collide and compress. Magnetic flux change in external coils enables direct electricity capture without thermal conversion. D-He3 fuel for near-aneutronic operation.
Quasi-isodynamic optimized stellarator with HTS magnets. 3D twisted coils produce helical field externally. No plasma current, no disruptions. Inherently steady-state.
Large stellarator building on W7-X heritage. Conventional (non-planar) coil design at power-plant scale. Steady-state, disruption-free.

Linear solenoid with magnetic mirror end plugs. Tandem mirror and gas-dynamic trap variants. Simple open geometry. Steady-state. End losses historically limiting but modern HTS and improved physics may resolve.
University / Lab Experiments: WHAM (UW-Madison), GDT (Budker Institute), TMX (LLNL, ended), GAMMA-10 (Tsukuba)

Description: Single superconducting coil levitated inside vacuum vessel creates dipolar magnetic field. Plasma confined in external region. Inspired by planetary magnetospheres. Steady-state, inherently MHD stable.
Ions orbit high-voltage cathode without grid. ExB electron confinement. Desktop-scale form factor. Hybrid electrostatic/magnetic confinement concept.
Magnetized plasma compressed by mechanically driven liquid metal liner. Pulsed at 1-10 Hz. Intermediate density/timescale between MCF and ICF.
University / Lab Experiments: LANL MTF (Theta Pinch + liner), HyperJet Fusion (plasma jet driven MTF)

Description: Axial current creates self-pinching magnetic field. Sheared axial flow stabilizes MHD instabilities. Pulsed/quasi-steady operation. Simple geometry, no external magnets.
University / Lab Experiments: FuZE (University of Washington), ZaP (UW), Sandia Z Machine (Z-pinch variant)

Description: Muon replaces electron in hydrogen molecule, shrinking bond length 207x and enabling room-temperature fusion. Real physics demonstrated. Energy balance challenge: muon production cost vs. fusion energy per muon lifetime (alpha sticking problem).
University / Lab Experiments: PSI (Switzerland), TRIUMF (Canada), ARPA-E BETHE program, RAL (UK)

Concept Name: Laser ICF - Direct Drive Fast Ignition (D-T)
Description: Laser-driven direct drive ICF with fast ignition architecture. Long-pulse DPSSL compresses cryogenic D-T capsule; petawatt-class CPA ignition pulse triggers burn. Distinguished from Xcimer's Hybrid Direct Drive (concept 27).
University / Lab Experiments: NIF (LLNL, indirect drive achieved Q>1), OMEGA (U. Rochester, direct drive), LMJ (France), SG-III (China)

Description: Field-reversed configuration optimized for proton-boron-11 aneutronic fuel. Near-unity beta FRC with neutral beam injection for plasma heating and current drive. Truly aneutronic (<1% neutrons) eliminates tritium breeding blanket, heavy shielding, and remote handling. Requires extreme confinement performance (150-300 keV). Direct energy conversion potential.

Compact HTS dipole coil deployed to LEO using vacuum of space as confinement vessel. Eliminates vacuum vessel (dominant loss channel in terrestrial dipoles). Plasma extends to magnetic separatrix (10-50 m). Claims confinement volume exceeding ITER for <$30M. Targets D-He3 for aneutronic operation. Power delivery via beaming partners.

Modular HTS Stellarator (QI-optimized). Building Infinity One demonstration stellarator with non-planar HTS coils, followed by Infinity Two pilot plant. Solid-breeder (HCPB) blanket. Steady-state, disruption-free.
Compact stellarator with laser-patterned HTS film on cylinders (novel manufacturing). Flowing liquid Li-LiH wall + Pb pebble multiplier (architectural hybrid). Steady-state.

Low aspect-ratio tokamak with HTS magnets. Higher plasma beta and more compact than conventional tokamak. Distinct physics regime from CFS ARC-class devices. Potential for smaller, cheaper devices at the cost of more challenging center-stack engineering.

Hypervelocity projectile compresses fuel target on impact. Electromagnetic launcher accelerates projectile to >70 km/s. Multi-cavity amplifier targets reach pressures to 10 TPa. Liquid Li curtain wall (TBR=1.8, validated TUV SUD UK Feb 2026) serves as integrated breeder/shield. Pulsed at sub-Hz (0.033 Hz pilot; 0.1 Hz commercial).
University / Lab Experiments: Sandia flyer plate experiments, First Light Fusion (Project Amp), Naval Research Lab (flyer plate ICF)

Description: Ultrashort-pulse laser irradiates engineered nanostructured solid targets (nanowires, foams, layered composites) containing p-B11 fuel. Enhanced laser absorption via nanostructure (potentially 80%+ vs 5-15% for smooth surfaces). Aneutronic. Room-temperature target handling, no cryogenics.
University / Lab Experiments: LFEX (Osaka, p-B11 alpha detection), NIF ARC beamline experiments, ELI-NP (Romania), Vulcan (RAL UK)

Description: Pulsed coaxial electrodes create dense, short-lived plasma pinch (plasmoid). Claims path to p-B11 net energy via extreme ion temperatures in the pinch. Very simple, compact device. Direct energy conversion of charged fusion products.
University / Lab Experiments: Various DPF devices worldwide (Chile, Poland, Singapore), NX2 (Singapore), PF-1000 (IPPLM Warsaw)

Description: Linear induction accelerator drives heavy ion beams to compress DT targets. Key advantage: 30-50% wall-plug efficiency vs 1-15% for lasers. Accelerator is inherently modular (hundreds of identical induction cells), enabling factory mass production. Direct-drive HIF targets.

Hybrid Direct Drive (HDD) laser ICF architecture. First pulse heats a hohlraum to generate X-rays that ablate the capsule and form a thick plasma atmosphere; subsequent pulses drive the capsule directly through this atmosphere. Excimer (KrF) laser system at 248 nm UV, ASPEN pulse compression, 10+ MJ. Distinct from conventional indirect drive (concept 31, Inertia) and conventional direct drive (concept 17, Focused Energy).
University / Lab Experiments: Phoenix laser (Xcimer, Jun 2025), Physics of Plasmas 31(11), 112708 (2024)

Description: Magnetic cusp confinement of electrons to create a deep electrostatic potential well that confines and accelerates ions. Combines magnetic and electrostatic confinement principles.
World's first full HTS tokamak (HH70). Achieved 1,337-second steady-state plasma in Feb 2026. Based in Shanghai. Building next-gen Honghuang 170 targeting demo power station ~2030.

Compact tokamak optimized for negative triangularity plasma shape. Higher confinement, disruption-resilient. Prototype called LUCIOLE. Franco-Swiss company collaborating with DIII-D National Facility. Targets early 2030s for burning plasma demo.

Laser-driven indirect drive ICF using a hohlraum to convert laser light to X-rays that compress a D-T fuel capsule. DPSSL (Thunderwall: ~1000 beamlines at 10 kJ each, 10 Hz, frequency-tripled UV; 10 MJ total). Building on Kritcher's NIF Hybrid-E target heritage. Founded by Jeff Lawson + Kritcher + Mike Dunne. $450M Series A (Feb 2026).

Laser-based IFE using novel Optical Enhancement Cavity (OEC) architecture. Founded by 2014 Nobel Laureate Dr. Shuji Nakamura (white LED inventor). Claims efficient, modular, reliable, cost-effective laser system. Based in Santa Barbara with offices in Silicon Valley and Tokyo.
Laser-driven ICF. Spin-off from Thales Group. Leading TARANIS project with CNRS and CEA. Winner of France 2030 program. Targeting 1000 MW power plant by 2050.

Developing BEST (Burning Plasma Experimental Superconducting Tokamak). Majority state-owned (CNPC, Chinese Academy of Sciences). Plans first plasma 2027, Q~5 by 2035. Part of China's national fusion strategy.
PoloMac concept for magnetic confinement. Swiss early-stage startup. 4th place Boldbrain Startup Challenge 2025.
Advanced nuclear fusion reactors using helical coil technology. Spun out from Japan's National Institute for Fusion Science (NIFS). Tokyo-based.

Magnetized Target Inertial Fusion (MTIF). Plasma armature railgun launches 50 gram projectiles at ~10 km/s into pure deuterium fuel targets that are magnetized upon impact. Confinement family is MIF (not IFE) because fuel is magnetized during compression. Distinct from concept 23 (First Light Fusion) which uses electromagnetic launcher at >70 km/s into D-T targets with no magnetization. D-D primary fuel; D-T listed as backup. Molten Pb first wall.

High-current particle accelerator drives beam-target D-T reactions to produce neutrons. Operating commercial neutron source since 2010 (medical isotopes including Mo-99, materials testing, radiation hardening services for industrial and defense applications). Non-power application — current revenue model is medical isotopes and irradiation services, not electricity. Future power-plant variant is possible but undisclosed. Blanket = N/A (non-power, not no-tritium): SHINE uses D-T fuel but does not breed tritium because they buy it commercially for the accelerator beam-target reactions.

Spherical tokamak with central-solenoid-free (CS-free) operation; non-inductive current drive via ECRH. Targeting proton-boron 11 fuel for aneutronic operation. Devices: EXL-50 (2019, R=50cm, 0.5 T), EXL-50U (first plasma Jan 2024, 1 MA / 1.2 T sustained), EHL-2 (target 2027, 3 MA). ENN's published roadmap: ENN's roadmap for proton-boron fusion based on spherical torus, Physics of Plasmas 31(6), 062507 (2024). Funded $400M by parent gas company; private-sector commercial fusion development.
